Key details:
- Issuing authority: Justervesenet (Norway), address Fetveien 99, N-2007 Kjeller, Norway. Notified body no. 0431. Person responsible: Mr. Alf Magne Andreassen. Phone (+47) 64 84 84 84, email postmottak@justervesenet.no, website justervesenet.no
- Certificate number: R129/2000-NO-06.03, Project number 04/1067-4164, Page total 2, Member State Norway
- Applicant: Mettler-Toledo Cargoscan AS, Norway, Grenseveien 65/67, N-0663 Oslo, Norway
- Manufacturer: same
- Certified type: "Dimensioner: Cargoscanner CND910, Display: Cargoscanner CS2200" — this is a dimension measuring system (R129 is "Retrofit table (dimensioning measuring instruments)"? Actually R129 is "Multidimensional measuring instruments"). Category: dimension measuring instrument. Type designations: CND910 (Dimensioner), CS2200 (Display).
- Class A: d ≤ 2 cm — accuracy class A with d ≤ 2 cm.
- Recommendation: R129, edition 2000, accuracy class A.
- Test reports: 
  - Norwegian Metrology Service, T01/2002, 72 pages
  - Norwegian Metrology Service, T01/2005, 73 pages
  - Norwegian Metrology Service, T07/2005, 76 pages
  - NEMKO, 42267 rev 1.0, 45 pages
- Date issued: 17 August 2006
- CIML member / signatures: Dr. Helge Kildal, Director General, Norwegian Metrology Service; Mr. Alf Magne Andreassen, Senior Engineer, Legal Metrology.
- Also references type-approval certificate N-23/2006-1068 — could be in description.

Characteristics: "Class A: d ≤ 2 cm" — this could be a type_level characteristic: accuracy_class: "A", scale_interval: d ≤ 2 cm. Let me record:
- accuracy_class: {value: "A"}? Actually recommendation has accuracy_classes: ["A"].
- scale_interval (d): value {min: null, max: 2}, unit "cm". "d ≤ 2 cm" → maximum_scale_interval? I'd record attribute "scale_interval" with value {max: 2} unit "cm".

The scheme: The cert doesn't state scheme A or B explicitly. OIML-CS scheme — older certificates under R129 2000 are basic OIML certificates of conformity, not scheme A or B. Leave scheme null or omit.

Components: The certified pattern has a "Dimensioner: Cargoscanner CND910" and "Display: Cargoscanner CS2200". These could be components: role "dimensioner" (measuring unit) with type CND910; role "display" with type CS2200. Or they could be type_designations. The schema has certified_type.type_designations[] for all type identifiers. I'll put both CND910 and CS2200 there, and also record components with roles.

model_family: only one model each; skip.

Description: "The characteristics and specifications are described in the test certificates involved" — that's boilerplate, not really a description. Could include the note about the type-approval certificate N-23/2006-1068. I might add description mentioning conformity of pattern represented by samples identified in test reports and type-approval certificate N-23/2006-1068. Probably fine to omit or include briefly. I'll include a short description: "Cargoscanner dimension measuring system consisting of dimensioner CND910 and display CS2200." Hmm — rule 8 says don't fabricate; but a description synthesizing from the doc is acceptable? Safer to include the type identification text as description. I'll set description to "Dimensioner: Cargoscanner CND910; Display: Cargoscanner CS2200. Class A: d ≤ 2 cm." Actually that duplicates other fields. Maybe include: "Conformity of the pattern represented by samples identified in the associated test reports and the type-approval certificate N-23/2006-1068." I'll include that.

oiml_issuer_id: Notified body no. 0431? That's a notified body number, not an OIML issuer ID. Justervesenet's OIML issuer ID might be different. I'll set oiml_issuer_id to null or omit. Hmm, could use "0431" but that's a notified body number. Safer to omit.

Category: R129 is "Multidimensional measuring instruments" — a dimensioner/cargoscanner measures parcel dimensions. Category could be "Dimension measuring instrument" or "Cargoscanner". I'll use "Dimension measuring instrument".
